close_reason: P3 / clippy::too_many_lines (pedantic, 118/100). Extracting the SSE state-machine closure into a free function would make it unit-testable separately from the live mock HTTP stream, which is a real benefit. But the closure has substantial async capture state (raw_buf, decode_buf, scan_from, the reqwest stream itself), and refactoring it without changing behaviour requires either a state-machine struct or a Pin<Box<dyn Stream>> adapter — non-trivial, with regression risk. Existing integration tests on the unfold loop are comprehensive. Deferring; revisit when the SSE state machine needs another change anyway, or when adopting clippy::pedantic in CI surfaces this lint as a real blocker.
description: src/client.rs:374-531 — clippy::too_many_lines (pedantic, 118/100). The fn body contains: URL validation, header injection, content-type check, then a multi-arm `unfold` closure containing the entire SSE state machine (delimiter scan, chunk fetch, raw_buf accumulation, UTF-8 decode, scan_from update, frame emit). The state machine is the largest single piece. Idiomatic Rust split: extract the closure body into a free function `fn next_sse_frame(state: SseStreamState) -> Future<Output=...>` so the public method is a thin orchestrator. This makes the state machine independently unit-testable (currently exercised only via integration tests on a live mock HTTP stream). Note: locked crate.
